title: Whole f45r Q1: ordered entries and occurrence-bound reprise with meanings unassigned
summary: EXPLORATORY ALTERNATIVE TO R1. The same86IT groups become three ordered specifications. Ordinary occurrences introduce separate positions with untranslated descriptions; field reprises bind a unique previous ordinary occurrence referent, not an entire paragraph subject. Doublets retain two semantic positions without selecting portions, actions or time.

design.phase: exploratory authorship; no new corpus experiment
design.fixed_lexing: Use the immutable R1 structural trace only: five free markers and five finite bound forms; all other whole forms remain opaque. Do not inherit R1 subject or identity assignments.

types.position: One ordered specification position per ordinary occurrence. Distinct positions are part of the proposed content, not merely saved source addresses.
types.referent: Each position has a referent; two positions may denote the same real entity. No physical distinctness, portion, action or time asserted.
types.description: The same unknown predicate N_w constrains both ordinary referents and field arguments.
types.field: Single value per marker per textual paragraph record, not per described object.

composition: Ordinary events append a fresh position with N_w(referent). Preserve all61 ordinary positions in their written order; no duplicate collapse.
Free and licensed bound fields apply the existing untranslated descriptor to their field argument; consumed hosts are not ordinary sequence positions.

For a field descriptor search exact ordinary occurrences in earlier completed paragraphs of this page. Zero matches leaves a variable; one occurrence binds its referent; multiple occurrences are unresolved, even within one earlier paragraph. Do not pick nearest or collapse repeated matches.
Current paragraph, embedded substrings, inferred properties and previous field arguments are not lookup candidates.
All occurrences of the same field in a paragraph constrain its one value. Later explicit binding unifies earlier variables and descriptions.
Physical line boundaries are retained source information, not new scope resets. No fixed event order, physical process or numerical unit is assigned.
new_assumptions: the paragraph encodes an ordered specification
ordinary occurrences are separate semantic positions
unique previous occurrence reprise replaces unique previous paragraph reprise
retained_assumptions: five free marker roles and five finite bound forms
known_limits: Positive unknown types still allow easy fit. Semantic order is stipulated, not independently identified.
Field-assertion order is not yet semantic; moving DALDAIIN earlier need not change final constraints.
No universal grammar:1047 paragraph-initial DAIIN remains a counterexample to universal postfix export.
R1 remains a published separate alternative; its constraints do not automatically carry over.

decision_note.positive_knowledge: Exact reader-stable CHOL/YKEOL doublets and separated OKAIIN occurrences; exact OPCHAL/OPCHALDY and DAL-family anchors; finite composition and preserved wholes.
decision_note.predecessor_unknown: R1 has a real symbolic joint parse but duplicate predicates and ordinary-event permutations often leave its final assertions unchanged. It has not explained final DALDAIIN placement.965 measured portions,1360 positive-duration phases and1145 incomplete membership are not native content bindings.
decision_note.outcome_decision: If a uniform occurrence-bound parse works, retain a concrete alternative with narrower referent constraints and meaningful repeated positions, while leaving lexical values unassigned. If it fails, retain the failure and R1; do not add arbitrary operator glosses or local reference exceptions.
decision_note.smallest_adequate_work: Align all86 existing groups once under declared alternative; manually read all3 paragraphs; independent source/identity accounting and publication. No additional corpus, reserve or decoder.
decision_note.wall_time_budget: 45 minutes total including the preceding bounded retrieval, authoring, validation and publication; stop expansion at checkpoint. No new statistical experiment or GDT ID.
predecessors: GDT1146/1147 failed fixed recipe binding/return chain
